name: Pike Push-Up
summary: A bodyweight vertical press in an inverted V position that trains the shoulders and triceps, and prepares you for handstand push-ups.
setup: Start on hands and feet with your hips high so your body forms an inverted V.
Place hands about shoulder width apart and feet hip to shoulder width apart.
Keep your arms and legs nearly straight and your head between your arms.
For an easier version, raise your feet less or put your hands on a low step.
execution: Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands.
Keep your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your body.
Pause just above the floor, then press the floor away to return to the start.
Keep your hips high throughout the rep.
mistakes: Hips dropping so it becomes a regular push-up: walk the feet closer and lift the hips.
Elbows flaring wide: keep them at about 45 degrees.
Bouncing off the head: lower under control and stop above the floor.
Too hard to complete reps: raise the hands on a sturdy chair or step to reduce load.
